 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2.

That on 07.06.2023 at about 3.15 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in a TVS XL 100 bearing No. KA-06-HF-4147, on Kesaramudu Haraluru Tar road, Jodikatte,
Bairasadra, Guluru Hobli, Tumakuru, when he reached near Basavanna Temple, at that time, driver of Ford Car bearing Reg.No.KA-22/MA-2529 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner came from opposite direction with high speed and dashed against the petitioner's TVS XL.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately he was shifted Aditya Hospital after first aid,
he was shifted to Hemavathi Hospital, Tumakuru wherein he took the treatment as an inpatient and spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards conveyance, nourishment,
medical expenses and other incidental charges.
4. It is stated that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 58 years and doing agriculture and labour work and earning Rs.45,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries, he could not able to do his work as earlier.
5. It is stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Ford Car bearing Reg.No.KA-22/MA-2529.
Hence, Kyathasandra Police have registered criminal case against driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.160/2023.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition,
seeking compensation.
6. After service of summons, respondent No.1 & No.2 appeared through their counsel & filed the written statement.
7. In the written statement, the respondent No.1 & 2 have contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner and not on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further denied the entire averments of the petition and also denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.

Ultimately, stated Nagendra H R vs Mohan Kumar on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26619646/
2 that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exaggerated and arbitrary.

sentences.text: With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1.
Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of Ford Car bearing No.KA-22-MA-2529 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the petitioners as stated in the claim petition?
3. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What Order or Award?
9. In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.

Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.B.Ramesh,
Orthopaedic Surgeon as PW2 and got marked the document at Ex.P15 and Ex.P16.
10.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has examined himself as RW1 and got marked two documents as Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.
11.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.

12. My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: Partly Affirmative Issue No.4: As per final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:-
13.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Ford Car bearing Reg.No.KA-22/MA-2529 the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

14. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 & 2, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, but seriously disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

3 15.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of the rival contentions of both the parties, on going through the above issue burden is on the petitioner to prove the above issue on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
16. The petitioner in order to prove his case got examined himself as PW1.
He has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon the police documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P8.

Ex.P1-copy of FIR, Ex.P2-true copy of FIS, Ex.P3-true copy of charge sheet, Ex.P4-true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P5-true copy of wound certificate,
Ex.P6-statement of petitioner, Ex.P7 - statement of mahazar witness and Ex.P8-true copy of IMV report.

17. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that based upon the first information statement given by Renukaradhya, registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the Investigation Officer of the case has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
18.
In support of the stand of the respondents, the respondent No.1 has examined as RW1.
But his evidence will not much helpful in order to believe the defences of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.

19. In the light of the evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Ford Car bearing Reg.No.KA-22/MA-2529 .
As such, the petitioner has placed the satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2 & 3:
20.
These issues are with respect to the age, income and entitlement of relief claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

21. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injuries cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.

The object of awarding Nagendra H R vs Mohan Kumar on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26619646/
4 compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

entities.text: Nagendra H R vs Mohan Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "While determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation."

Pain and Sufferings;
22.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.

In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate issued by Hemavathi Hospital,
which is marked as Ex.P5.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1.Comminuted subtrochanteric fracture shaft of right femur,
2.Comminuted subtrochanteric fracture shaft of left femur,
3.Comminuted proximal tibia fracture left 4.Left patella fracture,
5.CLW left eye brow 6.CLW left elbow 7.Multiple abrasion over body 8.Multiple soft tissue injury over body 9.3rd - 8th rib fracture right 10.
Bilateral nasal bone fracture 23.
As per the opinion of the doctor the injuries No.1 to 4, 9 & 10 are grievous in nature and ret of the injuries are simple in nature.
The petitioner has produced discharge summaries as per Ex.P13.
On perusal of discharge summaries marked at Ex.P13 issued by Hemavathi Hospital, which discloses that he was admitted from 07.06.2023 to 19.06.2023 and from 09.11.2023 to 11.11.2023.
Apart from his evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.B. Ramesh as PW2.

He has stated in his evidnce that the petitioner has sustaind Comminuted subtrochanteric fracture shaft of right femur,
Comminuted subtrochanteric fracture shaft of left femur, Comminuted proximal tibia fracture left,
Left patella fracture and 3rd - 8th rib fracture right.
He has placed outpatient record and x-ray at Ex.P15 & Ex.P16.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he might have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-
Nagendra

H R vs Mohan Kumar on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26619646/
5 under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
24.
PW1 has stated that, he was doing agriculture and also doing labour work and earning Rs.45,000/- per month.
In this regard, there is no iota of documents to show the income of the petitioner.
Hence, in the absence of the documents, it is apt to take the notional income as per law.
On perusal of discharge summaries marked at Ex.P13 issued by Hemavathi Hospital, which discloses that he was admitted from 07.06.2023 to 19.06.2023 and from 09.11.2023 to 11.11.2023.

During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to his to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of four months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.64,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
25.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses, he has produced medical bills to the extent of Rs.4,08,084/- along with prescriptions at Ex.P14.
Further RW1 has placed medical bills of Rs.16,500/- at Ex.R1 along with prescriptions at Ex.R2.
There are no contra materials available on record to disprove the medical bills.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,21,584/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
26.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summary the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as attendant charges.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
27.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW-1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P5 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injuries for which he took the treatment as an inpatient.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.B.Ramesh examined as PW-2.

PW-2 has stated in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained Comminuted subtrochanteric fracture shaft of right femur, Comminuted subtrochanteric fracture shaft of left femur, Comminuted proximal tibia fracture left, Left patella fracture and 3rd - 8th rib Nagendra H R vs Mohan Kumar on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26619646/
6 fracture right.
Further deposed that, Internal fixation right femur left femur, bone grafting internal fixation left tibia and other fractures treated conservatively.
28. Further stated that, radiological examination shows fracture left and right femur non union with implants in situ.
Left proximal tibia malunited with implants in situ other fractures united present.

Further, the doctor has assessed permanent physical disability of lower limb is at 78% and whole body disability is at 39%.
29.
At the time of cross-examination of PW2, admitted that he is not the treated doctor.

Further denied the suggestion that the fracture is not united due to the negligence of the doctor and also denied the suggestion that he has assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side to help the petitioner.
30. Over all appreciation of evidence of Doctor along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW2 as physical disability for limb is 78% and whole body is 39%.
Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW2, it is apt to take whole body disability as 24% instead of 39%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
31. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 58 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed any Aadhar card at Ex.P9 and D.L. copy at Ex.P11 for consideration.
On perusal of the said documents, his date of birth is mentioned as 15.02.1965.
The alleged accident occurred on 07.06.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 58 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '9' is to be taken into consideration.

32. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident he was doing agriculture and also doing labour work and getting an income of Rs.45,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not placed any iota of documents.
In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2023.

As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.16,000/- for the year 2023.
33.

In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.16,000 X12 X 9 X24/100= Rs.4,14,720/-.
Loss of amenities;
Nagendra H R vs Mohan Kumar on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26619646/
7 34.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries, he cannot discharge his duties effectively.

On perusal of evidence of PW1 and PW2 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities.

Future Medical Expenses;
35.
PW2 has stated that petitioner needs further treatment for non union of fracture and implant removal.
PW2 has not placed any estimation in this regard.

On going through the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the escalation of rates in the medical field, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of future medication.

36. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 1,00.000-00  2.Loss of income during laid- Rs. 64,000-00  up period and rest period  3.

Medical expenses Rs. 4,21,584-00  4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 15,000-00  and Conveyance Charges  5. Loss of future income due Rs. 4,14,720-00  to disability  6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 50,000-00  7.Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000-00
Total Rs.10,95,304
. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,95,304/-.
The respondent No.1 has paid Rs.16,500/- towards medical expenses of the petitioner.
The said amount has to be deducted.
After deducting the said amount it comes to Rs.10,78,804/-.

The petitioner is entitled for Rs.10,78,804/- (Rupees ten lakhs seventy eight thousand eight hundred and four only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016, between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S.
Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

sentences.text: As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Ford Car bearing Reg.No.KA-22/MA-2529 alleged accident had taken place.

The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1,
remained unshaken.
It is pertinent to note that, the respondents being the owners of the Ford car having no insurance policy.

As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owners of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6%
p.a. the petitioner from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 & 3 Partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.4:
39.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,78,804/- (Rupees ten lakhs seventy eight thousand eight hundred and four only) along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till the realization of the award amount.

The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.

After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this the 6th day of March 2026).
